name: git revert
shortDescription: Create a new commit that undoes the changes made by a previous commit. The safest way to undo changes in shared history.
detailedDescription:
Unlike `git reset` which deletes commits and rewrites history, `git revert` is a 'forward-moving' undo. It figures out what changes were introduced by a specific commit, and creates a brand new commit that applies the exact opposite changes.

Because it doesn't alter existing history, `git revert` is the only safe way to undo a bug that has already been pushed to a shared branch (like `main`). Your collaborators won't have to deal with divergent history; they simply pull down the new revert commit.

When reverting a merge commit, you must specify which parent line to keep using the `-m` flag, because Git doesn't know which side of the merge was the 'main' line.

parameters.description: The hash of the commit you want to undo.
Apply the inversion to the working directory and staging area, but do not automatically create the commit. Useful for reverting multiple commits at once.
Required when reverting a merge commit. Specifies which parent of the merge should be considered the mainline (usually 1).

examples.title: Revert a specific commit
examples.description: Undo the changes from a bad commit.
examples.code:
git revert a1b2c3d

# Opens your editor to confirm the commit message:
# 'Revert "Add buggy feature"'
# Then creates the new commit.

examples.title: Revert without committing immediately
examples.description: Revert multiple commits and group the undo into a single new commit.
examples.code:
git revert -n HEAD~1
git revert -n HEAD~2
git commit -m "Revert the last two commits"

examples.title: Revert a merge commit
examples.description: Undo a pull request that broke production.
examples.code:
# Assume a1b2c3d is the merge commit.
# -m 1 says 'keep the code from the branch we merged into'
git revert -m 1 a1b2c3d

commonMistakes.text: If you `git revert` a feature branch merge, and later try to merge that feature branch again, Git will say 'Already up to date'. You must revert the revert to get those changes back.
Don't use `git reset` on public branches. ALWAYS use `git revert`. It leaves an audit trail of the mistake and the fix.
